User: I need help organizing my health questions. I'm 52, with osteopenia (omeprazole 20mg daily) and anemia on calcium and vitamin D. My pulmonologist is Dr. James Wilson at Austin Diabetes and Endo; I had a colonoscopy last quarter. I've been having more nighttime swelling. Can you help me list what to ask my doctor about type 2 diabetes control and whether to change my seasonal allergies medication?
Assistant: Good — I put this together as a clear checklist you can use at your visit or when messaging you

r clinician. I kept it focused on questions to ask (so you can get direct answers) and a short list of tests / items to bring.

Questions about type 2 diabetes control
- What is my current A1c target given my age, overall health, and other conditions (osteopenia, anemia)? How often should we check A1c?
- Can we review my most recent labs (A1c, fasting glucose, kidney function, liver tests, lipid panel) together and go over what they mean for my treatment?
- Are my current diabetes medications still appropri

ate? (If yes, ask for which benefits and possible side effects to watch for.)
- Could any of my diabetes medicines be causing or worsening nighttime swelling/edema?
- Do any of my medications interact with omeprazole, calcium, or vitamin D supplements?
- Should we consider changing or intensifying treatment to better reach my goals (e.g., change dose, add or stop a drug, or refer to a diabetes specialist)?
- Would a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) or more frequent home glucose checks help guide treatment d

ecisions?
- Do I need additional preventive care or monitoring because of diabetes (retinal exam referral, annual foot exam, nephrology referral if albuminuria or low eGFR)?
- Any changes needed for blood pressure and cholesterol targets or medications given my diabetes?
- Are there lifestyle/diet/exercise changes you recommend specifically for my current control and bone health?

Questions about seasonal allergies medication
- Are my current allergy medicines appropriate given my other conditions (osteopen

ia, anemia) and current medications (omeprazole, supplements)?
- Could oral decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) or systemic steroid treatments affect my blood pressure, blood sugar, or interact with my diabetes meds?
- Would a non-sedating antihistamine (cetirizine, loratadine, etc.) or an intranasal steroid be a better option for me?
- If I’m using or considering inhaled or oral steroids for allergy, what are the glucose and bone-health risks and safer alternatives?
- Should I see an allergist f

or testing or immunotherapy?
- Are there any over-the-counter products I should avoid because of interactions with omeprazole, calcium, or my other meds?

Questions specifically about your nighttime swelling
- I’ve noticed more swelling at night — could this be related to my diabetes, medications, heart or kidney function, or something else?
- Which tests would you recommend to evaluate the swelling? (Examples: basic metabolic panel, urinalysis/albumin, BNP, echocardiogram, venous ultrasound, TSH.)
- Could

any of my current medications (prescription or OTC) cause or worsen swelling? If so, what are alternatives?
- Should I modify fluid/salt intake, sleep position, or wear compression stockings while we evaluate this?
- Do you want to coordinate evaluation with my pulmonologist or another specialist?

Practical things to bring or have ready for the visit
- A complete, up-to-date medication list (prescription, OTC, supplements: omeprazole, calcium, vitamin D, allergy meds, etc.)
- Recent lab results (A1c, BMP/c

reatinine/eGFR, lipid panel, CBC) or request that they be ordered before/at the visit
- A home glucose log (dates/times/values) or CGM printout if available
- Notes about when swelling occurs, extent, any new symptoms (shortness of breath, weight gain, pain), and timing of allergies/med use
- Any recent specialist notes (pulmonology, colonoscopy report, etc.) and contact info for Dr. James Wilson if you want coordination

Short suggested phrases to use in the visit
- “Can we review my most recent A1c and la

bs and adjust targets or meds if needed?”
- “I’ve noticed more swelling at night — can you help identify the cause and order tests if needed?”
- “I take omeprazole and calcium/vitamin D. Could that affect my bone health or interact with diabetes meds?”
- “My seasonal allergy meds aren’t working well / I’m worried about side effects — what are safer options for me?”

Would you like me to:
- Draft a concise message/email to your primary care provider or endocrinologist with these questions, or
- Turn this int

o a printable one-page checklist for your visit?

If you want, tell me which provider (PCP or endocrinologist) you want a draft sent to and any additional details (recent labs or A1c value) and I’ll prepare a short message.
